text: SWIFT is a training and inference framework for large language models and multimodal models. It supports supervised fine-tuning, pretraining, and reinforcement learning from human feedback.
Pretraining continues to train a language model on raw text with the causal language modeling objective. Every token in the sequence contributes to the loss, and no chat template is applied.

The causal language modeling objective predicts the next token given all previous tokens. The model learns the statistical structure of the corpus by minimizing the cross-entropy loss over the sequence.
A learning rate schedule warms up from zero and then decays, often following a cosine curve. Warmup stabilizes the early updates while the optimizer state is still being estimated.

Gradient accumulation splits a large logical batch into several micro-batches. The gradients of the micro-batches are summed before a single optimizer step, which emulates a larger batch on limited memory.
BF16 mixed precision stores weights and activations in the bfloat16 format. It keeps the exponent range of float32 while halving the memory footprint, which is stable for training.
Sequence packing concatenates several short documents into one fixed-length sequence. Packing raises the fraction of useful tokens per batch and avoids wasting compute on padding.
Data parallelism replicates the model across devices and splits the batch. Each replica computes gradients on its shard, and the replicas average the gradients before the optimizer step.
The tokenizer converts text into token identifiers. A byte pair encoding tokenizer merges frequent character sequences into subword units, which balances vocabulary size and sequence length.
Checkpointing saves the model weights and the optimizer state during training. A saved checkpoint lets training resume after an interruption and provides snapshots for evaluation.
Full-parameter training updates every weight of the model. It needs more memory than an adapter method but can fit new knowledge more thoroughly than a low-rank update.
The validation loss measures how well the model generalizes to data it did not train on. A widening gap between training and validation loss signals overfitting.
